case-1.objects: A finite index type ι, a measurable state space α, a family w assigning one fixed nonnegative real weight to each i : ι, a family κ assigning a kernel κ i from α to α to each i, and a measure μ on α. The finite-mixture kernel is the finite sum of the κ i after applying the constant density w i to each of them; for each state x and measurable event T its value is ∑ i, (w i : ℝ≥0∞) · (κ i)(x,T).
case-1.domains: The implicit types are ι and α, with instances [Fintype ι] and [MeasurableSpace α]. Weights are in ℝ≥0 (finite nonnegative reals), and are cast to ℝ≥0∞ for the densities and kernel-value arithmetic. The general definition permits a distinct measurable target β; the example specializes the target to α and does not independently quantify over β. The measure μ is in Measure α and the events in the integral interpretation are measurable subsets of α.
case-1.quantifiers: For every choice of ι and α and their indicated instances, every w : ι → ℝ≥0 and κ : ι → Kernel α α with [∀ i, IsSFiniteKernel (κ i)], and every μ : Measure α, the two hypotheses imply the conclusion. The s-finite instance and the invariance hypothesis each range over every i : ι, and all finite sums run over the whole index type. Invariance has an equivalent eventwise reading for every measurable T, with x integrated over α.
case-1.assumptions: Every component is an s-finite kernel and is invariant for the same μ, i.e. μ.bind (κ i) = μ for every i. The weights sum to 1 in ℝ≥0. Individual weights may be zero, and even zero-weight components are covered by both component hypotheses. No separate nonemptiness hypothesis is required: the normalization is impossible for an empty index type. Neither a finiteness or s-finiteness condition on μ nor a probability normalization of μ or the component kernels is assumed.
case-1.conclusion: The kernel finiteMixture w κ is invariant for μ: μ.bind (finiteMixture w κ) = μ as measures on α. Equivalently, for each measurable T ⊆ α, the nonnegative integral of x ↦ ∑ i, (w i : ℝ≥0∞) · (κ i)(x,T) against μ equals μ(T).
case-1.senses: Invariant means equality after integrating the kernel against μ, not a pointwise identity of kernel measures in the starting state. Integrals and kernel values use extended nonnegative arithmetic; μ(T) need not be finite. This is a one-way preservation statement for a finite mixture with fixed weights independent of source and target, not a result for state-dependent weights, a converse about the components, or a claim of probability normalization, uniqueness, convergence, ergodicity, or reversibility.
case-1.constants: The only numerical normalization is ∑ i, w i = 1 in ℝ≥0 (hence also after casting the finite sum to ℝ≥0∞). The density for summand i is the constant (w i : ℝ≥0∞), independent of both arguments, and zero weights are allowed. There is no bound on the number of indices other than finiteness and no additional rate, error, or mass constant.
